section_title: Should an unmarried believer seek marriage?

versions.label: BSB
paragraphs: 8 Now to the unmarried and widows I say this: It is good for them to remain unmarried, as I am. 9 But if they cannot control themselves, let them marry. For it is better to marry than to burn with passion.

context_lines: Paul addresses the unmarried and widows, commending remaining unmarried as he is. He also tells those who cannot exercise self-control to marry. Marriage is a permitted and good response, rather than a spiritual failure.

The counsel continues his recognition of different gifts. He is asking people to be honest about their circumstances and capacity, rather than trying to prove their devotion by adopting a way of life that leaves them struggling with temptation. These verses establish that Paul was unmarried when writing; they do not give a complete account of his earlier marital history.
common_interpretation_lines: Christians commonly understand this counsel as valuing unmarried service to God while permitting marriage and recognizing different gifts. The Catholic [Catechism 1618–1620](https://www.vatican.va/content/catechism/en/part_two/section_two/chapter_three/article_7/i_marriage_in_gods_plan.html) honors both marriage and virginity for the kingdom as gifts from the Lord; [Wesley’s note on verse 7](https://wesley.nnu.edu/john-wesley/john-wesleys-notes-on-the-bible/notes-on-st-pauls-first-epistle-to-the-corinthians/) likewise connects remaining unmarried with a gift not given to everyone.
god_plan_lines: In [Matthew 19:10–12](https://biblehub.com/bsb/matthew/19.htm), Jesus describes some people choosing to forgo marriage for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. He also says this is something only those given the capacity can receive.

This connection places voluntary singleness within service to God’s kingdom, rather than making it simply the absence of a spouse. Paul’s permission to marry also matters within that purpose: the call is to faithful service with the gifts one has received, rather than a single required household arrangement for every believer.
current_position_lines: We don't have a position on this passage yet. When our study reaches a conclusion the text supports, it will appear here.
